actor: White House OSTP frontier-AI executive-order signing-window coordinator
job: Stage the Frontier Model Review Board executive order for signing inside the OECD GENAI June 2-6 plenary window after the post-deadline signing posture opens.
outcome: Frontier Model Review Board executive order signed on a date falling between the OECD plenary opening session on June 2 and its closing read on June 6 with the CISA federal-civilian directive cited in the preamble as operational precedent.
motivation: An eight-of-eight classified-annex close inside the Friday May 22 deadline window converts the OSTP posture from indefinite into a signing window the order must clear inside the plenary horizon to keep the three-instrument architecture coherent.

task.who: White House OSTP interagency-review desk plus the National Security Council frontier-AI lead and the Office of the Staff Secretary signing-prep team
task.what: fold the now-complete classified-annex record into the order package and route it through the Staff Secretary signing queue
task.where: the White House OSTP interagency-review process and the Office of the Staff Secretary signing queue
task.when: from the Friday May 22 post-deadline session through the June 2-6 OECD GENAI plenary window
task.why: the post-deadline signing window has opened and the order has to land inside the plenary horizon
task.how: interagency review close plus Staff Secretary signing-prep package and preamble citation of the CISA directive

actor: OECD GENAI working-group secretariat working-procedure review lead
job: Run the working-procedure review on the draft Recommendation text across the eleven calendar days remaining to the June 2-6 plenary so the closing session can carry the United States recognition vote rather than deferring it to a post-plenary written-procedure round.
outcome: The sixteen-jurisdiction reciprocity perimeter recognizing the United States as the seventeenth named jurisdiction inside the plenary's closing session itself with the originating UK and EU on the same vote.
motivation: Holding the closing-session recognition vote inside the plenary keeps the reciprocity perimeter on the same operating session the executive order signs in, rather than slipping into a four-week written-procedure round that breaks the convergence story.

task.who: OECD GENAI working-group secretariat plus the sixteen named candidate delegations and the originating UK and EU delegations in active review
task.what: process working-procedure review comments across the second business day and the remaining seven business days into the plenary
task.where: the OECD GENAI working-group secretariat review channel and the June 2-6 plenary venue
task.when: from the Friday second business day of working-procedure review through the June 2-6 plenary closing session
task.why: the closing-session recognition vote is the perimeter's clearing step inside the plenary window
task.how: working-procedure review of the draft Recommendation text plus delegation comment intake and plenary scheduling

actor: House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Communications and Technology majority staff director
job: Hold the locked Wednesday May 27 morning subcommittee markup on the parallel 30-day technical-review joint resolution and circulate the Friday-morning supplemental staff memorandum covering the now-closed Senate classified-annex record.
outcome: The joint resolution clearing the May 27 subcommittee markup and advancing to full-committee markup inside Q3 2026 as the House-track companion to the executive order.
motivation: Keeping the House parallel-track instrument live alongside the executive order and the CISA directive is what preserves the three-instrument convergence the plenary closing-session recognition vote reads against.

task.who: House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Communications and Technology majority staff director and the amendment-drafting counsel team
task.what: circulate the Friday supplemental staff memorandum, run the Wednesday markup, and report the resolution to the full committee
task.where: the House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Communications and Technology markup room and the full-committee referral queue
task.when: from the Friday May 22 supplemental memorandum circulation through the Wednesday May 27 morning markup and the Q3 2026 full-committee window
task.why: the subcommittee-to-full-committee advance is the House-track clearing step that keeps the three-instrument set converging on the plenary window
task.how: supplemental staff memorandum circulation plus subcommittee markup process and full-committee referral

job: Transition the now-cleared n8n CVE-2026-21858 directive into compliance-monitoring mode against the eleven-CVE Trail of Bits agent-loader taxonomy so the executive order can cite it as a settled operational precedent in its preamble.
outcome: The CISA federal-civilian directive operating in compliance-monitoring posture across the Trail of Bits agent-loader taxonomy and named in the executive order's preamble as the executive-branch operational precedent.
motivation: A directive in compliance-monitoring posture on the same taxonomy the technical-review joint resolution references is what lets the executive order's preamble lean on a settled precedent rather than a forward-looking instrument.

task.who: CISA federal-civilian operational-directive program-management office and the attestation-intake operations team
task.what: validate bulk attestation submissions, stand up the compliance-monitoring dashboard, and confirm directive precedent language for the order preamble
task.where: the CISA federal-civilian operational-directive attestation-intake system and compliance-monitoring dashboard
task.when: from the Friday May 22 compliance-monitoring transition through the June 2-6 OECD GENAI plenary signing window
task.why: compliance-monitoring posture is what makes the directive a citable settled precedent inside the executive order preamble
task.how: attestation-intake validation plus compliance-monitoring dashboard stand-up against the Trail of Bits taxonomy

actor: OECD GENAI working-group United States recognition-gap rapporteur
job: Re-key the United States recognition-gap assessment to the now-three-instrument oversight stack (executive order, House joint resolution, CISA operational directive) ahead of the plenary closing-session recognition vote.
outcome: The reciprocity perimeter's recognition assessment circulated to the sixteen named candidate delegations plus the originating UK and EU keyed on the three-instrument US stack and reading clean against the closing-session vote.
motivation: Anchoring the recognition assessment on a fully instantiated US oversight stack closes the last open gap on the perimeter so the closing-session vote can carry rather than defer into the four-week written-procedure round.

task.who: OECD GENAI working-group United States recognition-gap rapporteur and the reciprocity perimeter assessment desk
task.what: revise the United States recognition assessment to read on the three-instrument stack and circulate the revised text to the working group
task.where: the OECD GENAI working-group reciprocity perimeter assessment channel and the June 2-6 plenary venue
task.when: from the Friday May 22 second business day of working-procedure review through the plenary closing session on June 6
task.why: a recognition assessment keyed on the fully instantiated stack is what the closing-session vote reads against
